This provides an overall calibration measure for a competing-risks model's predictions for a specific cause. **Use this to**: Reduce multiple cause-specific Brier scores (one per time point) to a single number for model comparison. Especially useful when comparing Fine-Gray models for the same cause with different covariate sets. **Interpretation**: Same scale as `brier_score_incidence()` (0 = perfect, 1 = worst). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A multi-state `Surv` response (from `gw.Surv()` with a categorical event). An `Outcome` or a formula response such as `'Surv(time, status == 2)'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. [incidence_prob]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Predicted cumulative incidence probabilities for the cause of interest, shape `(n_subjects, n_times)`. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Evaluation times (at least 2). The integrated Brier score is computed as the area under the Brier-score curve from `times[0]` to `times[-1]`, normalized by the time span. [cause]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The cause of interest (integer event code from the `Surv` response). [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `incidence_prob`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped first, along with the matching rows of any arrays passed alongside. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Integrated Brier score (time-averaged). Lower is better. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Summarize CIF calibration for progression (cause 1) into a single score using the `mgus2` dataset: ::: {#7c5cbc11 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw import numpy as np # The first of progression (PCM) or death, each with its own time and status columns mgus2 = gw.load_dataset("mgus2", backend="polars") first = gw.Outcome.first_event( endpoints={"pcm": ("ptime", "pstat"), "death": ("futime", "death")} ) # Marginal CIF from Aalen-Johansen as a naive baseline aj = gw.AalenJohansen().fit(first, data=mgus2) cif_df = aj.to_frame(format="polars") pcm_cif = cif_df.filter(cif_df["cause"] == "pcm") # Evaluate over a fine time grid times = np.linspace(30, 360, 12) marginal = np.array( [float(np.interp(t, pcm_cif["time"].to_numpy(), pcm_cif["estimate"].to_numpy())) for t in times] ) probs = np.tile(marginal, (mgus2.height, 1)) ibs = gw.integrated_brier_score_incidence( first, incidence_prob=probs, times=times, cause=1, data=mgus2 ) ibs ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.07514656777562731 ``` ::: :::
